Methodology

Each paper is scored on 9 dimensions (dataset availability, public access, framework-specific format support, code availability, clear metrics, data size, LLM evaluation presence, task type identifiability, and full text availability) weighted to a 10-point scale. Papers are tiered: Ready (8+), Possible (5–7.9), Barriers (2–4.9), Not Implementable (<2).

Generated 2026-03-12 from PDF extracts and paper metadata. See STATISTICS/ for full markdown reports.

Framework Profiles

lm-eval EleutherAI · lm-evaluation-harness

Community-standard harness with 200+ benchmarks. Supports multiple_choice, log-likelihood, and generate_until task types.

65 In Framework 178 Ready 413 Possible

Best for: reproducing published results; automated eval pipelines

Inspect UK AI Safety Institute · inspect_ai

Safety and alignment evals with model_graded_qa() scorer and rubric-based scenarios.

38 In Framework 23 Ready 29 Possible (model-graded)

Best for: safety/alignment evals requiring LLM-as-judge

LightEval HuggingFace · lighteval

Lightweight HF-native harness with easiest HuggingFace dataset integration. No “In Framework” tier.

99 Ready 771 Possible

Best for: teams in the HF ecosystem; fast iteration

HELM Stanford CRFM · helm

Holistic evaluation with scenario abstraction and broadest metric coverage.

16 In Framework

Best for: comprehensive multi-metric evaluation

OpenAI Evals OpenAI · evals

JSONL registry with templates (Match, ModelBasedClassify, FreeForm). All 2,043 papers scored.

783 Ready 872 Possible

Best for: structured community contributions; judge-based evals

Papers already implemented in at least one of the six evaluation frameworks. Identified by cross-referencing CEI vault papers against each framework’s task registry, benchmark lists, and integration documentation. These 107 papers represent benchmarks with confirmed existing implementations — the strongest candidates for immediate ethics-focused evaluation work.
Full cross-framework implementability matrix covering all 2,043 papers. Each paper is scored on 9 dimensions (dataset availability, public access, framework format support, code availability, clear metrics, data size, LLM evaluation presence, task type identifiability, and full text availability) weighted to a 10-point scale. Tier assignments: Ready (8+), Possible (5–7.9), Barriers (2–4.9), Not Implementable (<2).
The same implementability matrix as Tab 2, overlaid with ethics classification scores from the CEI pipeline. This view highlights which ethics-relevant papers are most actionable for framework integration — combining technical implementability with normative relevance to prioritize evaluation development.

lm-eval-harness

EleutherAI’s lm-evaluation-harness — the most widely adopted open-source LLM evaluation framework. Papers were matched against the harness task registry by benchmark name, dataset identifier, and task type.
